findings.title: Accounts vulnerable to AS-REP Roasting
findings.description: 1 enabled user account(s) have Kerberos pre-authentication disabled (userAccountControl DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH). Any unauthenticated user on the network can request an AS-REP for these accounts and attempt to crack the returned hash offline to recover the account password.
findings.mitre_attack: T1558.004 — Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: AS-REP Roasting
findings.recommendation: Re-enable Kerberos pre-authentication for every affected account unless a specific, documented legacy application requires it. Where it cannot be disabled, ensure the account uses a long, random password (25+ characters) that is not feasible to crack offline.

findings.title: Kerberoastable service accounts
findings.description: 1 enabled user account(s) have a Service Principal Name (SPN) set, meaning any authenticated domain user can request a Kerberos service ticket for them and attempt to crack it offline. 1 of these also belong to more than one group, which is worth checking for privileged membership.
findings.mitre_attack: T1558.003 — Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting
findings.recommendation: Set long, random passwords (25+ characters) on every service account, rotate them on a defined schedule, and prefer Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA) for any new service account, since gMSA passwords are machine-managed and effectively immune to offline cracking.

findings.title: Weak domain password policy
findings.description: The default domain password policy has the following weaknesses: minimum password length is 8 characters (recommended: 14+); passwords never expire.
findings.recommendation: Raise the minimum password length to at least 14 characters, keep complexity enabled, and set a bounded maximum password age. For accounts protected by MFA, consider NIST 800-63B's guidance to favor length over forced periodic rotation.

findings.title: Privileged group membership sprawl
findings.description: 1 tier-0 group(s) exceed 5 members: Domain Admins (7 members). Each additional member is a full domain-compromise path if their account is breached.
findings.control_reference: NIST 800-53 AC-6(1) (Least Privilege — Authorize Access to Security Functions) / CIS Control 5.4
findings.recommendation: Review the membership of every group over the 5-member threshold and remove any account that doesn't require standing privileged access. Consider just-in-time privileged access (e.g. time-bound group membership) instead of permanent membership for administrators who only need it occasionally.

findings.title: Stale or unused enabled accounts
findings.description: 1 enabled account(s) have not logged on in over 90 days (lastLogonTimestamp is a replicated approximation, so actual staleness may be greater).
findings.control_reference: NIST 800-53 AC-2(3) (Disable Inactive Accounts) / CIS Control 5.3
findings.recommendation: Disable accounts with no legitimate recent activity, and put a periodic access review in place so stale accounts are caught and disabled automatically rather than discovered during an audit.
